scenes.heading: Mendelian genetics
scenes.sub: Predicting inheritance, and testing it with statistics
scenes.say: Mendel's pea plants showed that genes are passed on following predictable rules. Let's apply them, test real data, and see where simple ratios break down.

scenes.heading: Mendel's two laws
points: Segregation: two alleles split into gametes
scenes.say: Segregation splits partners: the two alleles of a gene go to different gametes, giving three to one in a monohybrid cross. Independent assortment shuffles the deck: different genes are dealt out independently, giving nine, three, three, one. That's just two three to one ratios multiplied together.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Is the coin at the footy toss dodgy? 54 heads in 100 is normal
scenes.science: Chi-square asks: is the gap between O and E just chance?
scenes.breaks: A small χ² never proves the hypothesis is right; it only shows the data are consistent with it. Always use raw counts.
scenes.say: Flip a fair coin a hundred times and fifty-four heads is normal wobble. But eighty heads makes you suspicious. The chi-square test asks the same about a cross: is the gap between observed and expected counts just chance?
scenes.caption: Flip a fair coin 100 times and 54 heads is normal wobble. But 80 heads makes you suspicious. The χ² test asks the same about a cross: is the gap between observed and expected counts just chance?

scenes.heading: The chi-square test
scenes.say: Chi-square is the sum of O minus E, squared, over E. Degrees of freedom are classes minus one. Small chi-square, fits. Big chi-square, quits: reject the null hypothesis.
scenes.caption: χ² is the sum of (O − E)² over E. Degrees of freedom are classes − 1. Small χ², fits. Big χ², quits: reject the null hypothesis.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: 556 seeds: 315, 108, 101 and 32 in the four classes. Do they fit 9 : 3 : 3 : 1?
scenes.say: Five hundred and fifty-six seeds fall into four classes. Work out expected counts from the nine, three, three, one ratio. Chi-square comes to zero point four seven. With three degrees of freedom, the critical value is seven point eight one. It's smaller, so we fail to reject the null hypothesis.
scenes.caption: 556 seeds fall into four classes. Work out expected counts from the 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio. χ² comes to 0.47. With 3 degrees of freedom, the critical value is 7.81. It's smaller, so we fail to reject H₀.

scenes.heading: Linkage
points: Genes on one chromosome are inherited together
Test cross: the big two are the parents
scenes.say: Linked genes sit on the same chromosome. In a test cross, the big two classes are the parents and the small two are recombinants. Recombination frequency is recombinants over total, times one hundred. One percent is one map unit, and it never passes fifty percent.

scenes.heading: Two twists

left.title: X-linked recessive
points: Mum to son, never Dad to son

scenes.say: Two twists. X-linked recessive traits, like colour blindness, are far more common in males, who have only one X. They pass mum to son, never dad to son. In epistasis, one gene masks another: in Labradors, double recessive e dogs are yellow, giving nine, three, four.

points: χ² = Σ (O − E)² ÷ E, df = classes − 1
scenes.say: Recap. Three to one, and nine, three, three, one. Chi-square tests the fit. Recombination frequency gives map distance. X-linked traits go mum to son. And a modified ratio that still adds to sixteen means epistasis. Now try the practice questions!
